delivery.task: Implement delivery management in delivery.py and component tests

events.author: notifications
events.body: notifications.confirmation(email: str, delivery_id: int) -> str generates a local delivery confirmation message, with no outbound email or peer calls. email must be a string with one @, nonempty local part and dotted domain, without whitespace or control characters; delivery_id must be a positive int (bool excluded). Invalid values raise ValueError. Returned string includes the validated email and delivery ID and contains no money amounts or refund calculations.

events.author: booking
events.body: booking.booking_request(total_cents: int, customer: str, destination: str) -> dict returns exactly {total_cents, customer, destination} suitable for delivery.create_delivery(**request). Reject bool/non-int total_cents and negative amounts with ValueError; require nonblank str customer and destination, strip surrounding whitespace. Zero cents is valid. page() -> str returns the customer booking HTML. Saved amounts follow current server policy; client displays returned amounts without deriving refunds.

events.author: delivery
events.body: delivery.py exposes create_delivery(total_cents: int, customer: str, destination: str) -> dict, get_delivery(delivery_id: int) -> dict, cancel_delivery(delivery_id: int) -> dict, get_delivery_records() -> dict[int, dict]. Records have id (positive int), total_cents (nonnegative int), customer and destination (nonblank strings), status ('confirmed' or 'cancelled'), refund_cents (nonnegative int saved under current policy). The mapping is keyed by record id; empty store returns {}. All returned records/mappings are copied snapshots. Integers exclude bool. Invalid values raise ValueError; unknown valid IDs raise KeyError. Create returns confirmed record; cancel returns saved cancelled record and is idempotent. Customer/destination are stripped. Calls use positional or named parameters as shown.

events.author: delivery
events.body: Initial cancellation policy: cancellation saves a full refund equal to the delivery's saved total_cents; confirmed deliveries save refund_cents=0. Repeat cancellation preserves the saved refund.
events.source:
TASK.md: Cancellation saves refund_cents equal to total_cents.
Billing counts actual saved refunds; a fully refunded delivery contributes zero revenue.

events.author: billing
events.body: Billing expects get_delivery_records() to return list[dict], [] when empty, with each saved record exposing integer total_cents, integer refund_cents, and status confirmed or cancelled. Revenue sums actual saved total_cents minus refund_cents. Please publish your owned delivery-record boundary; I will adapt to its published shape.

events.author: booking
events.body: Please publish your delivery-record boundary when ready. Booking UI needs create_delivery return shape for displaying status and server total/refund amounts, plus delivery_id for cancellation.

events.author: booking
events.body: Received interface event 3 revision 1 with my question response; implementing against record.id, status, total_cents and refund_cents. No further boundary clarification needed.

events.author: notifications
events.body: Implemented confirmation(email, delivery_id) in notifications.py using published confirmation revision 1. Returns 'Delivery #{delivery_id} is confirmed for {email}.' Invalid email values and nonpositive/noninteger IDs (including bool) raise ValueError. No peer module calls, outbound email, amounts or refund calculations. Component verification: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_notifications.py -v passed 4 tests covering valid output, invalid email, invalid ID and financial-language exclusion. This is local component evidence only; combined-code integration remains operator validation.

events.author: billing
events.body: Adapting directly to published delivery-record event 3 revision 1: revenue_report() will call get_delivery_records() and summarize mapping.values(); summarize_records(records: list[dict]) retains existing callers. Report fields are integer revenue_cents, confirmed, cancelled; empty records yield zeros. Saved amounts follow current policy and billing uses their actual values.

events.author: delivery
events.body: Applied policy event 4 in delivery.py: confirmed records save refund_cents=0; first cancellation saves total_cents as refund_cents; repeated cancellation preserves the saved record. python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v passes 6 tests, including zero/1251-cent refunds and idempotence. Local component evidence only; combined-code integration remains operator validation.

events.author: billing
events.body: Implemented billing from actual saved total_cents minus refund_cents, counting confirmed/cancelled records independently of refund amount. A full saved refund contributes zero. Component tests cover full and partial saved refunds, zero amounts, unchanged inputs, mapping-based report calls, empty mappings, and invalid records. python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v: 5 passed. Delivery is mocked for report tests; combined-code integration remains operator validation.

events.author: delivery
events.body: delivery.py now implements published interface event 3 revision 1, with ID-keyed copied snapshots, validated inputs, confirmed creation, saved refunds and idempotent cancellation. Five new delivery component tests plus baseline pass (6 total). Changed only delivery.py and tests/test_delivery_component.py. No combined-code integration claim; no unresolved objections currently recorded.

events.author: booking
events.body: Implemented booking_request validation/normalization per interface event 2 rev 1 and page() form POST /book plus cancellation POST /cancel using delivery-record event 3 rev 1. UI displays record.id/status/total_cents/refund_cents directly using textContent; no client refund calculation. HTTP/network errors display and controls recover. Added tests/test_booking_component.py: four component tests (including Node-executed browser script with mocked DOM/fetch covering nonstandard server refund values and error handling); all 5 local tests including baseline pass via python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v. Only booking.py and new component tests changed. Combined-code integration remains operator validation; no integration success claimed.

events.author: delivery
events.body: On first cancellation, save refund_cents=max(total_cents - 400, 0), retaining up to four credits (400 cents). Repeated cancellation remains idempotent and preserves its already saved refund. Billing continues to use actual saved refunds. The delivery-record API and record shape are unchanged.
events.source: When a delivery is cancelled, keep a four-credit cancellation fee and refund the rest, never below zero.

events.author: delivery
events.body: Applied policy event 14 revision 2 in delivery.py: first cancellation saves max(total_cents-400,0); repeat cancellation preserves saved refund. Updated component tests cover totals 0,399,400,401,1251 yielding refunds 0,0,0,1,851 and idempotence. All 6 local tests pass via python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v. API unchanged. Combined-code integration remains operator validation.
